question: Q05

prior_assessment.note: The LSJ/DGE/LS(Gr.) data check out (Logeion; lsj.gr via WebFetch). DGE cites Gr.Naz. M.36.116C 'ἀδύνατον καὶ ἀνεγχώρητον ποιεῖν τι τὸν υἱόν', 'cf. Hsch.' and Sch.Hermog. Rh. 7.135. No lexicon records a dative or an attributive construction. The step to option a (the main recension's τῇ δὲ ἀριθμητικῇ τοῦτο ἀδύνατον) is an inference, though a sound one.

'Attested only as an Egyptian land tax' is wrong. DGE gives subst. τὸ ἀ. 'número cardinal' (D.T. 636.15, 637.25; Sch.D.T. 243.1). Sophocles p. 246 has 'numeral, applied to the cardinal numbers' (D.T. 636,15 ὄνομα; Herodn.). LSJ II cites a predicative neuter (Dam. Pr. 117), and the scholia have 'ἀριθμητικὸν γάρ ἐστι' (of ἕξ). The conclusion still holds: no sense means 'arithmetically' or 'for arithmetic'. On d: the adverb is idiomatic with verbs, but no instance with ἀδύνατον was found.

Confirmed and extended. Lampe p. 131 lists Gr.Naz. or. 30.11, Ps.-Ath. disp. 10 (M.28.449A) and Chrys. hom. 38.4 in Jo. In three of the six attestations the word is paired with ἀδύνατον (Gregory, Chrysostom, Sch. Hermog.). Reading P's clause as a rewording of τῇ δὲ ἀριθμητικῇ τοῦτο ἀδύνατον remains an inference.
Logeion LSJ: Adv. -κῶς Plu. QConv. 643c, Theo Sm. p. 116 H. Both passages were opened: Plutarch 643c 'ἀριθμητικῶς οὐ γεωμετρικῶς ὁρίζων', and Theon p. 116 'ἀριθμητικῶς τρισὶν ὑπερέχων'.

Smyth §1021 says a substantivized attributive adjective 'generally' takes the article. The §1039 example is οἱ ὑμέτεροι δυσμενεῖς, with the article. None of the six attestations of ἀνεγχώρητος uses it as a substantive with an attributive adjective: all are predicative. The analysis 'an arithmetical impossibility' is grammatically conceivable but has no parallel.
Now verified through Logeion (Bailly 2024): 'ἀνεγχώρητος, ος, ον, inadmissible, impossible, Naz. 8, 255'.
Logeion Bailly 2024: ἀριθμητικός 'qui concerne les nombres … ἡ ἀριθμητική (s.e. τέχνη) … habile à compter'; ἀριθμητικῶς 'numériquement, Plut. M. 643c'.
The gloss is correct. The bearing on b ('a neuter impossible thing, qualified by ἀριθμητικόν') is not supported by Bailly or by any attestation.

Smyth §341: the adverbial neuter accusatives cited are πολύ, μικρόν, πρῶτον, τήμερον, πολλά, all of quantity, order or time. Relational -ικός adjectives form adverbs in -ικῶς. Little bearing on the question.
Consistent with the Logeion LSJ/Bailly text.
Bailly entry confirmed (Naz. 8, 255). Correct that no dative complement is recorded.

The text of Smyth §1039 is verified, but its example has the article and a masculine person. The application to an anarthrous neuter predicate ἀνεγχώρητον has no attestation. Every use found is predicative and paired with or equivalent to ἀδύνατον.
§§1606–1609 are general (manner, measure, degree). Nothing in them supports an adverbial ἀριθμητικόν.

new_findings.source: Lampe, Patristic Greek Lexicon, p. 131, s.v. ἀνεγχώρητος (page image, archive.org leaf n177)
new_findings.found: 'ἀνεγχώρητος, impossible ἀδύνατον καὶ ἀ. ποιεῖν τι τὸν υἱόν, ὧν οὐ ποιεῖ ὁ πατήρ Gr.Naz.or.30.11(p.123.6; M.36.116C); ‡Ath.disp.10 (M.28.449A); Chrys.hom.38.4 in Jo.(8.222B).' No construction with a dative or an attributive adjective is recorded.
new_findings.how: Gives the full patristic attestation. Every instance is predicative and synonymous with ἀδύνατον. This removes the lexical basis for b's 'arithmetical impossibility' analysis but does not choose between a, c and d.

new_findings.source: Gregory of Nazianzus, Or. 30.11, ed. Mason (1899), First1KGreek tlg2022.tlg010
new_findings.found: 'οὕτως ἀδύνατον καὶ ἀνεγχώρητον ποιεῖν τι τὸν υἱόν, ὧν οὐ ποιεῖ ὁ πατήρ'. The same chapter classifies impossibilities and has 'ὃ τῇ φύσει μὲν ἀδύνατον, θεῷ δὲ δυνατὸν βουληθέντι'.
new_findings.how: ἀνεγχώρητον = ἀδύνατον. In the very passage where the word occurs, the domain or agent of (im)possibility is a dative (τῇ φύσει, anarthrous θεῷ) after a relative pronoun, the same frame as ὅπερ … ἀριθμητικῇ ἀνεγχώρητον. It equally allows a dative of the person (c).

new_findings.source: Ps.-Athanasius, Disputatio contra Arium 10, PG 28.449A (page image, archive.org patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_028, leaf n231)
new_findings.found: 'Ἐὰν τοῦτο ἀποδείξῃς, ὅπερ ἀνεγχώρητόν ἐστι, τάχα κἀμὲ ποιήσεις τῷ σῷ φρονήματι ἐπακολουθῆσαι.' The Latin version renders it 'quod sane fieri non potest'.
new_findings.how: The nearest construction to P's ὅπερ … ἀνεγχώρητον: a relative with a predicative ἀνεγχώρητον, not qualified by any adjective. It shows the predicate needs no noun to agree with, which tells against reading ἀριθμητικόν as an attribute.

new_findings.source: Ps.-Athanasius, Disputatio contra Arium 20, PG 28.461C, with footnote (23) (page image, leaf n237)
new_findings.found: 'Εἰ οὖν ἀνεγχώρητον δύο βασιλεῖς φῆσαι ἐπὶ βασιλέως ἑνός …'. Note (23): 'Mox idem et Basiliensis, Εἰ οὖν ἀνεγχείρητον.'
new_findings.how: A predicative use with an infinitive. The variant ἀνεγχείρητον shows that this rare word is itself exposed to scribal alteration.

new_findings.source: Ps.-Athanasius, Disputatio contra Arium 31, PG 28.480D (page image, leaf n246)
new_findings.found: 'διὰ τὸ ἀνεγχώρητον ἐπ᾽ ἀνθρώπου ἐκλαβεῖν τινα ἑτερούσιον τὸν βραχίονα'. The Latin version renders it 'quia nimirum in homine concipi non potest'.
new_findings.how: The only attested qualifier of the domain of ἀνεγχώρητον is a prepositional phrase, ἐπί + genitive. No adjective or adverb is used.

new_findings.source: John Chrysostom, Hom. 38.4 in Jo., PG 59.216–217 (page images, archive.org patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_059, leaves n216–217)
new_findings.found: 'τοῦτο λέγει, ὅτι Ἀδύνατον καὶ ἀνεγχώρητόν ἐστιν ἐμὲ ποιῆσαί τι ἐναντίον τῷ Πατρί.'
new_findings.how: A third pairing with ἀδύνατον, with accusative + infinitive. It confirms the word is a plain synonym of ἀδύνατον, so P's clause matches the main recension's τῇ δὲ ἀριθμητικῇ τοῦτο ἀδύνατον.

new_findings.source: Scholia in Hermogenis Status, Walz, Rhetores Graeci 7.1, p. 135.24–25 (page image, archive.org p1rhetoresgraeci07walzuoft, leaf n146)
new_findings.found: 'ἀδύνατον γὰρ εἶναι τοῦτο καὶ ἀνεγχώρητον'. Also p. 136.27–28: 'ὅπερ ἐπὶ τῶν πλαστῶν στοχασμῶν οὐκ ἐγχωρεῖ γενέσθαι', where the domain is again ἐπί + genitive.
new_findings.how: A fourth pairing with ἀδύνατον, predicative, with τοῦτο as subject: τοῦτο … ἀδύνατον καὶ ἀνεγχώρητον mirrors the main recension's τοῦτο ἀδύνατον.

new_findings.source: Sophocles, Greek Lexicon of the Roman and Byzantine Periods, p. 160 s.v. ἀνεγχώρητος; pp. 246–247 s.vv. ἀριθμητικός, ἀριθμητικῶς (page images)
new_findings.found: 'ἀνεγχώρητος, ον, (ἐγχωρέω) = ἀχώρητος. Pseudo-Athan. IV, 449 A.' 'ἀριθμητικός … numeral, applied to the cardinal numbers. Dion. Thr. 636, 15, ὄνομα … Herodn. … 2. Arithmetical. Athenag. Legat. 6, λόγος.' 'ἀριθμητικῶς, adv. numerically. Plut. II, 643 C. Hippol. Haer. 264, 38.'
new_findings.how: Sophocles' gloss 'ἀχώρητος' is contradicted by the passage he cites (Latin: 'quod sane fieri non potest'). Besides 'arithmetical' (λόγος), the entry gives only the grammatical sense 'numeral' and lists no adverbial use.

new_findings.source: Logeion: LSJ, DGE, Bailly 2024, Pape s.vv. ἀνεγχώρητος, ἀριθμητικός, ἀριθμητικῶς
new_findings.found: DGE ἀριθμητικός: '• subst. τὸ ἀ. número cardinal op. ordinal, D.T.636.15, 637.25, Sch.D.T.243.1'; '3 τὸ ἀριθμητικόν contribución … Egipto'; 'II adv. -ῶς … ἀ. οὐ γεωμετρικῶς … Plu.2.643c, ἀ. τρισὶν ὑπερέχειν Theo Sm.116'. LSJ II: 'τὸ ἓν ἁπλῶς οὐκ ἦν ἀ. Dam. Pr. 117'. ἀνεγχώρητος: LSJ 'impossible, Sch.Hermog.'; DGE 'imposible' (Gr.Naz., Hsch., Sch.Hermog.); Bailly 'inadmissible, impossible, Naz. 8, 255'; Pape 'unzulässig, unmöglich, Sp.'
new_findings.how: Answers the neuter lead. Besides the tax there is a grammatical sense ('cardinal numeral') and a predicative 'numerical'. None gives 'arithmetically' or 'for arithmetic', so b has no lexical support in that sense.

new_findings.source: Scholia in Odysseam 9.246 (and Herodian, Prosodia Odysseaca), First1KGreek tlg5026.tlg007 / tlg0087.tlg008; Scholia in Isocratem (vetera), tlg5028.tlg001
new_findings.found: 'τὸ ἓξ δασυντέον· ἀριθμητικὸν γάρ ἐστι'. Scholia on Isocrates: 'τοῦτο μὲν γὰρ ἀριθμητικόν ἐστι τὸ σχῆμα'.
new_findings.how: The only predicative neuter ἀριθμητικόν found means 'a numeral' or 'enumerative', not 'arithmetically'. A predicative ἀριθμητικόν in P would naturally read 'numerical', which makes no sense with ἀνεγχώρητον. This tells against b.

new_findings.source: Corpus search, accent-insensitive regex over all Greek XML in OpenGreekAndLatin First1KGreek (master zip) and PerseusDL canonical-greekLit (master zip): all forms of ἀριθμητικῶς
new_findings.found: 26 hits counting duplicate editions. Theon p. 116 H.; Iamblichus, De comm. math. sc. 32 ('περὶ τῶν τεττάρων στοιχείων γεωμετρικῶς ἢ ἀριθμητικῶς ἢ ἁρμονικῶς'); Proclus, In Remp. II (Kroll), 'δεικνύσθω δὲ … ἀριθμητικῶς' and 'ἀριθμητικῶς μὲν οὑτωσὶ … γεωμετρικῶς δέ'; Plutarch, QConv 643c; Hippolytus, Ref. (twice); Simplicius, In Phys.; Syrianus, In Metaph.; Anon. in EN; Pindar scholia. In every case the adverb modifies a verb or participle (show, consider, treat, exceed), often against γεωμετρικῶς. Never with ἀδύνατον, ἀμήχανον or an equivalent.
new_findings.how: d is the idiomatic form for 'in the arithmetical way' as opposed to the geometrical, but no attested pattern adverb + adjective of impossibility was found.

new_findings.source: Proclus, In Rempublicam, ed. Kroll, vol. II p. 38 (First1KGreek tlg4036.tlg001 opp-grc1, page markers)
new_findings.found: 'οὐ γὰρ ἔστιν ἀριθμὸν λαβεῖν τετράγωνον τετραγώνου διπλάσιον … (αὐτὸ τοῦτο γὰρ ἀδύνατον)'. This is the same mathematical fact as in P (32 is not square).
new_findings.how: The ancient statement of this impossibility uses no discipline adjective, adverb or dative. It does not discriminate between the options.

new_findings.source: Euclid, Elements VII.31 (Heiberg; PerseusDL tlg1799.tlg001 perseus-grc2); Heron, Metrica I.18 (Schöne p. 50; First1KGreek tlg0559.tlg006)
new_findings.found: Euclid: '… ὧν ἕτερος ἑτέρου ἐλάσσων ἐστίν· ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἀδύνατον ἐν ἀριθμοῖς.' Heron: 'ἐπεὶ ἐν ἀριθμοῖς οὐκ ἔστιν εὑρεῖν τετράγωνον τετραγώνου πενταπλάσιον'.
new_findings.how: The standard technical idiom for 'arithmetically impossible' is relative ὅπερ + ἀδύνατον + ἐν ἀριθμοῖς. None of the four options follows it. It shows only that ὅπερ … ἀδύνατον/ἀνεγχώρητον + qualifier of the domain is a natural frame.

new_findings.source: Galen, De constitutione artis medicae ad Patrophilum 12, Kühn I 264–265 (First1KGreek tlg0057.tlg006)
new_findings.found: 'ἀλλὰ τινὰ μὲν τῇ φύσει, τινὰ δὲ τοῖς ἰατροῖς ἐστιν ἀδύνατα … ἀδύνατον ὀρθῶσαι …, τῷ δὲ ἰατρῷ δυνατόν. … ἰατρῷ μὲν ἐμβαλεῖν δυνατόν, ἀδύνατον δὲ τῇ φύσει. … τῇ φύσει μέν ἐστι δυνατόν, ἀδύνατον δ᾽ ἰατρῷ'.
new_findings.how: A clear parallel for ἀδύνατον with a dative of the agent or power (τῇ φύσει), which is the type of the main recension's τῇ ἀριθμητικῇ. It is equally a parallel for an anarthrous dative of the practitioner (ἰατρῷ), the type of c. It supports a and c alike and favours neither b nor d.

new_findings.found: 'ταὐτὸ γὰρ ποιήσει … ἐπὶ μεγεθῶν μόνον, τῷ δ᾽ ἀριθμητικῷ ἐπ᾽ ἀριθμῶν.'
new_findings.how: The dative of ὁ ἀριθμητικός, 'the arithmetician', is standard, so the form c requires is available. The parallel is for the form only, not for its use with ἀδύνατον.

new_findings.source: Galen, De alimentorum facultatibus 1.2, Kühn VI 454; Aspasius, In EN p. 136 Heylbut (First1KGreek tlg0057.tlg037, tlg0615.tlg001)
new_findings.found: Galen: 'ὥσπερ ἐν γεωμετρίᾳ καὶ ἀριθμητικῇ συνεφωνεῖτο πάντα'. Aspasius: 'οἷον ἐν γεωμετρίᾳ καὶ ἀριθμητικῇ ἃς ὁ μὴ παραδεξάμενος …'.
new_findings.how: An anarthrous dative ἀριθμητικῇ naming the discipline is attested. Option a's missing article (P elsewhere has ἡ ἀριθμητική, τῇ γεωμετρίᾳ) is therefore no real objection, although these instances follow ἐν.

new_findings.source: Corpus search (same corpora): adjective or adverb in -ικ- immediately before ἀδύνατ-, ἀμήχαν-, ἀνεπίδεκτ- or ἀνέφικτ-
new_findings.found: Hits: Alexander, In An. Pr. ('ὧν δεικνυμένων συλλογιστικῶς ἀδύνατον ἦν λαβεῖν'); Galen, In Hipp. Aph. ('ἀναχυθῆναι τὴν χολὴν κριτικῶς ἀδύνατόν ἐστιν'); Galen, De crisibus ('ἐξευρεῖν ἔργον τι τεχνικὸν ἀμήχανόν ἐστι'). In each the -ικῶς belongs to the verb or participle and the -ικόν agrees with a noun (ἔργον).
new_findings.how: There is no parallel anywhere for 'X-ικόν ἀδύνατον' as 'impossible in respect of X' (b), nor for 'X-ικῶς ἀδύνατον' as 'X-ly impossible' (d).

new_findings.source: Package evidence, evidence/section-3.json: Vincent pp. 338, 340 with footnotes (P's readings)
new_findings.found: P's recorded scribal errors: τὸν τῶν ἀριθμόν for τὸ τῶν ἀριθμῶν (338 n. 2: added ν, ω>ο); τοῦ for τῆς (n. 4); τέμνει for τέμνειν (n. 5); διαστήματα for διαστημάτων (340 n. 3); κεκρυμμένων for κεκραμένων (340 n. 4). In P's own wording the antithesis to our clause is 'ἡ μὲν ἀριθμητικὴ … οὐ δύναται' (338.15–16) and 'Τῇ γεωμετρίᾳ δὲ τοῦτο ῥάδιον' (338.21), and P has an anarthrous practitioner, 'γεωμέτρης λαβών' (338.22), where H, Par. and V have 'ὁ γεωμέτρης μεταλαβών'.
new_findings.how: P's scribe demonstrably corrupts case endings, including -ῶν > -όν and an added ν, so ἀριθμητικόν assimilated to ἀνεγχώρητον is a plausible error. P's own dative-of-discipline antithesis (τῇ γεωμετρίᾳ … ῥάδιον) points to a. The ο/ω + ν pattern and the anarthrous γεωμέτρης are the best case for c.

decisive: Nothing is decisive. No reference work or text attests ἀνεγχώρητος with any of the four forms, or with a dative, an attributive adjective or an adverb. All six attestations are predicative, three of them paired with ἀδύνατον: Gr. Naz. Or. 30.11; Ps.-Ath. Disp. 10, 20, 31; Chrys. hom. 38.4 in Jo.; Sch. Hermog. The lexical evidence only establishes that ἀνεγχώρητον = ἀδύνατον. The choice of a over c rests on the parallel with the main recension (τῇ δὲ ἀριθμητικῇ τοῦτο ἀδύνατον) and on P's own antithesis (Τῇ γεωμετρίᾳ δὲ τοῦτο ῥάδιον), which is internal evidence, not reference evidence.

No corpus hit or web-search result quoted or discussed the Quadrivium of 1008, Heiberg's edition or Ps.-Psellus. I did not open or use any edition, transcription or translation of this text. I put no Greek phrase of the text into a search engine; I searched only single words (ἀνεγχώρητον with author names, ἀνεγχώρητος with 'Lexikon byzantinischen Gräzität'), with no hit on this text. The only material from the text itself that I used is the package evidence (Vincent pp. 338/340 and the facts in questions.json).
